bank.prompt: Brisbane's Old Windmill was built to grind grain using wind power — but it barely caught a breeze. What did authorities use instead to keep the millstones turning?
bank.reveal: Built in a windless spot, the mill never worked properly. Convicts were forced onto a treadmill — sometimes in leg irons — for up to 14 hours straight to grind the colony's grain.

source.title: Old Windmill Tower | State Library of Queensland
source.verifierNote: Page states 'it is located in a somewhat windless location, it quickly became a place of punishment, with convicts being put to work on a treadmill to keep the arms and heavy millstone turning' and that convicts wore 8kg leg irons for 14 hours.

bank.prompt: The Eternal Flame burning inside the Shrine of Remembrance at Brisbane's Anzac Square holds a rare national distinction. What is it?

options.label: It was the first eternal flame lit in Australia
It was the first war memorial built in Queensland

bank.reveal: Lit on Armistice Day, 11 November 1930, the flame at Anzac Square was Australia's first eternal flame — beating Melbourne's Shrine of Remembrance by 24 years.

source.title: Eternal flames in Australia | Australian War Memorial
source.verifierNote: Page states 'Australia's first eternal flame was lit in Brisbane on Armistice Day in 1930' and that Melbourne's second eternal flame was lit by the Queen in 1954.

bank.prompt: Which came first at the site of Toohey Forest Park — the Toohey family settling their cattle property, or the Commonwealth acquiring part of the land for a post-war Soldiers Settlement?

options.label: The Toohey family settling Mount Galway

bank.reveal: The Toohey family occupied 'Mount Galway' from 1872. The Commonwealth only acquired the first section of the park in 1919, for a proposed WWI Soldiers Settlement.

source.title: Toohey Forest Park | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states: 'the Toohey family from 1872 to 1946' and 'The Commonwealth acquired the first section of the park in 1919 for a proposed post World War 1 Soldiers Settlement.'

bank.prompt: Which came first at the Kedron Park Hotel in Wooloowin — the hotel opening its doors, or the brick extension added along Lutwyche Road?
bank.reveal: The Kedron Park Hotel was built in 1881 for owner Frederick Morris. The brick extension on the Lutwyche Road frontage wasn't added until 1920, under James Cavill's ownership.

source.title: Kedron Park Hotel | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states: 'The Kedron Park Hotel was built in 1881' and 'Under ownership of the James Cavill a brick extension was added on the Lutwyche Rd frontage in 1920.'

bank.prompt: The heritage-listed 'Dutch Houses' built in Sunnybank in the early 1950s were unusual for Brisbane because they were constructed from what material?
bank.reveal: Built 1951–55 by a joint Australian-Dutch company, the Sunnybank Dutch Houses used concrete tiles popular in the Netherlands — a method previously unused in Brisbane, where timber was the norm.

source.title: Dutch Houses | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states houses were 'constructed using a form of concrete wall tiles previously unused in Brisbane' and built between 1951 and 1955 by joint Australian-Dutch company Concrete Developments Pty Ltd.

bank.prompt: The heritage-listed house 'Primrosa' in Nundah was built in 1912. According to its heritage listing, what was the suburb of Nundah originally known as?
bank.reveal: The suburb was named 'German Station' after Lutheran missionaries who settled there from 1838. The name changed to 'Nundah' — believed to be an Aboriginal word for a chain of waterholes — when the railway arrived in 1882.

source.title: Primrosa | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states 'The suburb of Nundah was originally known as German Station' and that the name changed to 'Nundah' when the railway was built in 1882.

bank.prompt: Brisbane's Tattersalls Club building on Edward Street was designed by the same architectural firm as which other famous Brisbane landmark?
bank.reveal: Both were designed by Hall & Prentice. The Tattersalls clubrooms opened in 1926, the same firm having completed City Hall in 1930.

source.title: Tattersalls Club - Wikipedia
source.verifierNote: Page states the building 'was designed by Hall and Prentice' and separately states Tattersalls Club 'was formed in November 1883'; the History & Heritage page at tattersallsclub.com.au explicitly calls Hall and Prentice 'the architects responsible for Brisbane City Hall'.

bank.prompt: The heritage-listed car park on Wickham Terrace in Spring Hill holds an unusual distinction — what was it the first of?

options.label: The first parking station built by Brisbane City Council
The first underground car park in Queensland

bank.reveal: Designed by City Architect James Birrell and completed in 1960, it was BCC's first-ever parking station — and was heritage-listed in 1995. A tunnel connects it to Central Railway Station.

source.title: James Birrell, Queensland architect | State Library of Queensland
source.verifierNote: Page explicitly states 'It was constructed between 1959 and 1960 and was the first parking station constructed by the Council' and that it was added to the Queensland Heritage Register in January 1995.

bank.prompt: The Brisbane suburb of Teneriffe got its unusual name from a landowner in the 1850s. What did he name it after?

options.label: The largest of the Canary Islands
A Scottish coastal village he grew up near

bank.reveal: Property speculator James Gibbon named his 1854 land holding after Tenerife, the largest island in the Canary Islands archipelago — giving the suburb its distinctive double-F spelling.

source.title: 46 Kingsholme Street, Teneriffe | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states: 'Gibbon's naming of Teneriffe was a variation of Tenerife, the largest island in the Canary Islands archipelago.'

bank.prompt: Newstead House — Brisbane's oldest surviving residence, built in 1846 — served a special civic role for several years. What was it?
bank.reveal: From 1853 to 1859, Captain John Wickham hosted government business at Newstead House, making it the colony's unofficial government residence before a formal one was established.

source.title: Brisbane River Heritage Trail | Brisbane City Council
source.verifierNote: Page states: 'The oldest surviving residence in Brisbane, it served as the unofficial government house between 1853 and 1859.'
